correctness.rationale: Squaring and subtracting gives the Walsh polynomial (4); its constant and distinct degree-two coefficients give exactly (5), in both directions. For two nonzero half-sums u,v a nonzero coordinate in just one support would give a nonzero off-diagonal coefficient by pairing it with the support of the other vector. On the common support the ratios v_i/u_i are nonzero and pairwise opposite, so there are at most two indices; orthogonality excludes just one. The two ratios being opposite and u·v=0 give equal absolute coordinates in u and then the stated symmetric/antisymmetric form for u and v. For a fixed pair, equality under the anchor is equivalent to annihilating either half-sum, i.e. a_i=±a_j; a tied pair is independently witnessed by e_i,e_j, and unequal absolute coordinates can be chosen for every d. The absolute difference of |p+q| and |p−q| in magnitude is 2 min(|p|,|q|); applied to the anchor it gives the lower bound 1/sqrt(2) times the minimum absolute-coordinate gap (divide by 2 sqrt(2) min(|alpha|,|beta|)). Coordinate vectors attain it, including when the gap vanishes. The separate compactness argument for positive global stability is sound: scaling both half-sums to unit length bounds the squared quotient from below, and a zero on the product of spheres would give a nontrivial collision. 'One additional non-flat measurement' means an appropriately chosen row satisfying (2), not every non-flat row; the precise iff statement already specifies this.
residual_risks: Real full sign frame only; no random subframe, complex uniqueness, or identification of the exact global Lipschitz constant. Finite checker is not the all-dimensional proof.

evidence: The general completion theorem indeed implies one generic added row suffices: the smallest maximum of the ranks of complementary sign-row spans is d−1. A parity split attains it, and any subspace of rank r contains at most 2^r cube vertices by projection to r independent coordinates, excluding a cover by two subspaces of rank ≤d−2.
The inspected independent-variable stability and subgaussian settings do not give a stable all-real-sign-frame theorem with this single arbitrary deterministic row.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On lifting, the kernel of the full sign measurements on symmetric matrices is trace-zero diagonal, and the relevant differences of outer products have rank at most two. This explains why the exact fibers are very structured: the nontrivial rank-two differences have exactly two diagonal entries of opposite sign. Prior isolated collisions or a general injectivity test do not themselves give all the half-sums or the separation quotient.

value.rationale: The all-signal obstruction of the natural maximal flat real frame is known, but describing precisely how it fails identifies every offending direction and provides an exact deterministic design condition for the cheapest completion. The restricted margin gives a calibration quantity for just the formerly indistinguishable signals, with attained witnesses, while distinguishing it from full-map conditioning. This is a usable structural and quantitative result beyond a generic existence theorem or an isolated collision.
residual_risks: No exact full-map conditioning, arbitrary noise model or recovery algorithm is established.
